rules: Intraday range (high-low) normalized by price or dollar volume produced two of this round's top three fitnesses (3.481 and 1.952). This price_volume sub-family is worth continuing to push on.

Use ABS($return), not signed $return, when correlating against volume or dollar_volume. The signed version failed the cheap screen (|t| 0.40) while the absolute-return version was this round's second-best factor (fitness 2.523).

Fast-turnover entries were this round's two weakest accepted factors (0.486 and 1.027) despite clearing the bar. Turnover charges appear to hit quick-decay price_volume signals hardest, so slow/medium-horizon variants are currently the better trade in this niche.

Rank or raw forms of $dollar_volume are saturating the archive: TS_RANK($dollar_volume,21) and raw $dollar_volume were both rejected for over 0.93 correlation with existing archive members. A new volume-level proposal needs a transform that isn't just another monotonic reshaping of the same series.

Ratios with only $dollar_volume in the denominator risk collapsing into a proxy for dollar_volume itself: ABS(return)/dollar_volume was rejected for 0.90 correlation to a dollar_volume moving average. Give the numerator comparable dynamic range, or normalize the denominator too.

Skip short-vs-long volume moving-average ratios (e.g. 5-day over 63-day); one such ratio failed the cheap screen (|t| 0.29). Same-window dispersion (std/mean at one lookback) is the pattern that actually passed (fitness 1.027).

Don't graft a whole small fundamental subtree (e.g. RANK($roa)) onto an unrelated technical branch under one top operator. Two crossovers doing exactly that were rejected as sharing only 2 nodes with the fundamental parent, i.e. not a real fusion.

Fundamental-technical fusions land better when both sides are normalized the same way: the one accepted mixed-niche entry ranked both branches (CS_RANK x TS_RANK), while the two rejected ROA crossovers combined a bare rank with a raw price ratio or an IF_ELSE gate.

equities, fitted on 2000 to 2013.

Below is what happened in the round just finished on this island: which
proposals were accepted into the archive with their fitness, and which were
rejected with the reason. Fitness is a t-statistic of the mean daily rank IC,
scaled by year-to-year stability and charged for complexity and turnover.

  fitness   1.027  niche fast/price_volume/low  TS_STD($dollar_volume, 63) / (TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 63) + 1e-8)
  fitness   1.878  niche fast/price_volume/high  ($volume - TS_MEAN($volume, 21)) / (TS_STD($volume, 21) + 1e-8)
  fitness   2.523  niche slow/price_volume/low  TS_CORR(ABS($return), $volume, 10)
  fitness   0.486  niche fast/price_volume/low  CS_RANK(TS_SUM(SIGN($return) * $volume, 21))
  fitness   1.952  niche medium/price_volume/low  TS_MEAN(($high - $low) / ($open + 1e-8), 63)
  fitness   3.481  niche slow/price_volume/low  TS_MEAN(($high - $low) / ($dollar_volume + 1e-8), 10)
  fitness   1.193  niche medium/mixed/high  CS_RANK($accrual_gap) * TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 21)

REJECTED
  TS_MEAN(ABS($return) / ($dollar_volume + 1e-8), 10)
      correlation: |rho| 0.902 >= 0.80 against `TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21)`
  TS_MEAN($volume, 5) / (TS_MEAN($volume, 63) + 1e-8)
      cheap_screen: |t| 0.29 < 1.00 on the cheap window
  TS_CORR($return, $dollar_volume, 21)
      cheap_screen: |t| 0.40 < 1.00 on the cheap window
  TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 21)
      correlation: |rho| 0.942 >= 0.80 against `($volume - TS_MEAN($volume, 21)) / (TS_STD($volume, 21) + 1e-8)`
  RANK($roa) * (TS_MIN($low, 21) / ($close + 1e-8))
      crossover_not_a_fusion: shares only 2 nodes with `RANK($roa)`
  IF_ELSE(RANK($roa) > 0.5, TS_MAX($high, 21) / ($close + 1e-8), 0)
      crossover_not_a_fusion: shares only 2 nodes with `RANK($roa)`
  $dollar_volume
      correlation: |rho| 0.935 >= 0.80 against `TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21)`

over windows under 5 days were rejected for low coverage" beats "prefer robust
factors". Do not restate the hard limits, which are already enforced. Do not
propose expressions here.
